frequency_question: How often does the bureaucratic and legal machinery required to lift an embargo complete within 365 days?
membership_rule: Includes any executive order, royal decree, or legislative enactment formally rescinding a state's complete ban on trade and financial transactions with a specific target nation. Excludes partial waivers, sector-specific exemptions, or unannounced tacit resumptions.

cases.name: US lifting of trade sanctions on Myanmar
US lifting of trade and financial sanctions on Sudan
Resumption of UAE-Qatar trade and transport ties after Al-Ula agreement
Resumption of Saudi-Iran diplomatic and commercial normalization steps
ECOWAS lifting of economic sanctions on Niger
US partial lifting of Syria sanctions for earthquake relief (partial/miss for full lift)

coverage_note: 6 named cases; representative of modern rapid diplomatic normalization and sanctions removal events.
known_gaps: Excludes confidential bilateral arrangements where decrees are not officially published.
skeleton: Executive decree preparation (14 days) + inter-agency regulatory alignment and banking compliance circular drafting (30 days) + customs system reconfiguration and port/air corridor clearance protocol updates (30 days) + public notification and grace period (15 days). Total sequential time: 89 days.
multiplier: Max required procedural duration (89 days) < available calendar window (365 days)
validity_reason: Administrative speed for digital-era regulatory updates remains stable across modern state apparatuses.
